title: core: cargo workspace + virus-core rules engine + snapshot + parity foundations
description:
GOAL: cargo workspace scaffold + virus-core rules engine, the foundation every other crate depends on.

SCOPE:
- Workspace with crates virus-core, virus-eval, virus-search, virus-mcts, virus-proto, virus-arena, vsbot (bin) — only virus-core implemented, others are empty stubs so the workspace builds. CI workflow (GitHub Actions): fmt, clippy -D warnings, test.
- virus-core: State (rows/cols up to 50x50, default 12x12, 2-4 players), Cell{owner,kind} packed as u8, bases at P1(0,0) P2(rows-1,cols-1) P3(0,cols-1) P4(rows-1,0), 3 actions/turn, Move + PlaceNeutrals actions, legality (8-adjacency to base-connected component, BFS over 8-neighbours of own cells), capture => YOUR Fortified, neutrals: two OWN Normals, once/game, only at movesLeft==3, consumes whole turn. Elimination after every action (no legal move => inactive; cells STAY, remain capturable). Winner = last active; outcomeWinner territory tiebreak for capped games (port from Java GoState.outcomeWinner).
- Board is 144 bytes at 12x12 — a flat [u8; N] copy per apply is fine and simpler than make/unmake; do NOT copy the Go/Java pattern of re-running full-board elimination BFS per player per node naively — hoist scratch buffers into a reusable workspace like Go's evalWorkspace.
- Incremental Zobrist hash covering cells + current + movesLeft + neutralUsed.
- Position layer (port of Go position.go / Java GoPosition): cached connectivity+frontier, ForEachSearchAction, strategic neutral-pair curation (<=48 pairs via Tarjan articulation classes with reserved quotas) when moves + C(owned,2) > 32.
- CRITICAL: move enumeration ORDER must match Go/Java exactly (row-major target scan etc.) — search parity in the next bead depends on identical child ordering. Read Go game/position.go and Java GoPosition side by side.
- Snapshot decode (serde): tolerant of owner/Owner, kind/Kind, string and numeric kinds; full validation port of Go game/snapshot.go FromSnapshot; defensively recompute activity (server Active[] bug: eliminated seats owning cells reported active).

REFERENCE CODE (read, port, do not invent): ~/Project/virusgame/backend/game/{state.go,position.go,snapshot.go}; ~/Project/nnue-trainer/src/main/java/com/engine/nnue_trainer/search/gobot/{GoState.java,GoPosition.java}.

ACCEPTANCE:
- cargo test green incl.: decode every state in fixtures/gobot_search_parity.jsonl (412 records) without error; legal-move counts and enumeration order spot-verified against the Java implementation on at least 20 fixture states (write a small Java or manual cross-check, or derive expected ordering from the fixture's recorded best-move indices); transition unit tests for capture-fortifies, neutral-consumes-turn, elimination-cells-stay, territory tiebreak.
- Benchmark: apply+undo (or apply-copy) and movegen ns/op recorded in the PR description.
- CI green on the PR.

LANDMINES: see ARCHITECTURE.md invariants 1,4,5. Do not add search or eval code here — core only.
notes: Draft PR #1 opened (vsbot-e7f-core-rules-engine), CI green. Workspace + virus-core rules engine complete; 39 tests. New oracle fixtures/gobot_movegen_order.jsonl (412 records, generated by linking the real Go engine) pins enumeration order, legal counts, FNV-1a stateHash and post-apply successor hash; 111 records cover the curated neutral-pair branch. Codex P1 triaged as invalid (Go json tag wins over field name; verified by marshalling the real backend) and pinned as a regression test instead. Bench in the PR body. Deferred: no eval/search work; non-corner base layouts only covered via round-trip.
close_reason: Merged PR #1: cargo workspace (7 crates), CI (fmt/clippy/build/test), complete virus-core rules engine with 412-record golden parity vs the REAL Go engine (enumeration order + state hash + successor hash, incl. 111 Tarjan neutral-pair records), tolerant snapshot decode pinned against literal server bytes. Benchmarks: apply 235ns, movegen 723ns. Deferred: non-corner base layouts only round-trip tested; Position::new_with untuned (12 Tarjan passes at turn start — profiling target for the search bead).

title: gen-8: recipe attack — curriculum x3, completed-Q target, per-head epochs, ragged targets
description:
Gen-8: attack the TRAINING RECIPE, not data volume. Two consecutive kept-backs (gen-6 0.480/100 window=1; gen-7 0.480/400 window=2, 0.55 OUTSIDE the interval, instrument control 0.850) prove more same-recipe data does nothing (top-1 moved 0.3pt for 2x rows). The Java pipeline promoted 5 straight generations with the SAME trainer — the differences are the levers, in priority order:

1. HUMAN-GAMES CURRICULUM x3 (the one big thing Java's gen-5 had that our runs lack). Source: prod games.db — NOTE the WAL trick: the public export https://vs.wandergeek.org/data/games.db is frozen at the last checkpoint; fetch games.db AND games.db-wal side by side and sqlite replays the WAL on open (see vsbot-p2y notes). Port the HumanCurriculumEmitter pattern (nnue-trainer scripts/mcts_selfplay_gen.sh stage): replay human-involved 12x12 games, deep-search each multi-choice position with the champion (CURRICULUM_SIMS raised to exploit Rust speed), emit rows (pv=root visits, z=real outcome absolute), repeat x3. Owner games vs SuperiorBot get extra repeats (positions where the champion demonstrably failed — incl. the (8,8)+(11,10) probe class, fixtures/probes).
2. COMPLETED-Q POLICY TARGET on the PUCT arm (PR #33's key finding: it is a transform property, needs no Gumbel; raw halving visits are WORSE). Emit improved-pi rows; A/B one generation trained on completed-Q vs raw visits.
3. PER-HEAD EPOCHS (gen-7: value loss still falling @8, policy top-1 peaked @6): either two-phase training or early-stop policy head; small trainer-side change, keep schema.
4. RAGGED POLICY TARGETS in the trainer (92% padding, k=326 vs mean 25) — unlocks WINDOW=3 (357k rows OOMs at 5.5GB today) AND 10x memory. Python-side change in nnue-trainer's train_selfplay.py — this is the one place "trainer unchanged" should bend; keep the row schema untouched.
5. Fix selfplay p1-skew (578/422 in gen-7's rounds — check tau/noise interaction with first-mover advantage).
6. Value-target reweighting on the neutral-probe position class (vsbot-07x close: value head is the culprit; probe set = regression measure per generation).

Machinery ready: trainer/generation.sh (memory-capped, resumable), rows byte-reproducible from seeds 5011/6011/7011 (~3h to regenerate 357k rows), arena --a-net/--b-net for Gate A, probe tool for the neutral class. Gate: 0.55/400 fixed-sims vs gen-5, then Gates B + C auto-promotion per docs/CANARY.md.

title: gen-7: 3-round window accumulation -> train -> 400-game gate
description:
Gen-7 with the data-breadth fix from gen-6's diagnosis (see vsbot-ml6 close + trainer/reports/gen6.md): gen-6 trained on ONE generation of rows (117,973); gen-5's own promotion used a 3-generation window. Fill the window locally: run TWO more 1000-game self-play rounds with the gen-5 champion (Dirichlet on, distinct seed bases spaced >=1000 from 6011 and each other), pool all three row sets (~350k rows) via the WINDOW=3 mechanism in trainer/generation.sh, train at champion geometry, gauntlet 400 colour-paired fixed-sims games vs gen-5 (box permitting per the lock convention — T2 cell is DONE, lock free), report per the standard.
Gate: pooled >=0.55/400 -> Gate A pass -> proceed to Gate B (vs ab-enhanced + Go bot via fixed harnesses) + Gate C automated live soak per docs/CANARY.md; auto-promote on all three per the no-gatekeeper policy. <0.55 -> KEPT BACK with diagnosis (loss curves, entropy, holdout top-1 vs gen-6's 61% plateau) — and the next lever is curriculum from prod games.db (S5 scope).
Numbers to trainer/reports/gen7.md + bead + PR.
notes:
EXECUTOR FINDING (blocking deviation, gen-7 run): gen-6's self-play rows are GONE. trainer/reports/gen6.md points at work/gen6/ inside the gen-6 executor's worktree (.claude/worktrees/agent-a982e020ae9e98f24) — that worktree has been cleaned up, and /home/devbox/Project/vsbot/work/ did not exist at all. Both the 117,973 rows and gen-6's candidate.json are unrecoverable.

Consequence: 'two more rounds + gen-6's rows' cannot fill a 3-generation window. Running THREE 1000-game rounds instead, so the window is actually ~350k rows as the bead intends. Seeds 5011 / 6011 / 7011 (SEED_BASE=11 + GEN*1000, pairwise >=1000 apart; derive_game_seed is a mix64 hash so streams are uncorrelated). Seed 6011 reconstructs gen-6's own row set at its own seed; 5011 and 7011 are the two NEW rounds the bead asked for.

Rows now land in the MAIN checkout /home/devbox/Project/vsbot/work/ (durable, gitignored) as window slots gen5/gen6/gen7 for GEN=7 WINDOW=3 — NOT in a temp worktree, so gen-8 can actually reuse them. work/gen5 is a window slot, not the historical Java gen-5 data; a PROVENANCE note records that.

Cost: +1h self-play. Will be stated in trainer/reports/gen7.md.
EXECUTOR FINDING 2 — the 3-generation window does not fit in RAM on this box.

Measured (not estimated) in vsbot-trainer:cpu, reproducing train_selfplay.py's exact memory behaviour on gen-7's real rows: PEAK 1.85 GB at 119,161 rows, k=326. Linear in rows:
  ~1.9 GB @ 120k (1 gen)  fits
  ~3.7 GB @ 236k (2 gens) fits
  ~5.5 GB @ 354k (3 gens) does NOT — box has 7.7 GB total, ~5.45 GB available, NO SWAP.

Why it is so heavy: train_selfplay.py is not streaming. It holds the parsed row dicts + train tensors + holdout tensors + a per-epoch 'shuffled = [t[perm] for t in train_t]' copy that overlaps the previous epoch's, so tensors are resident ~3x at each epoch turn. And the policy target is (n, k) with k = dataset MAX legal actions (326) vs a MEAN of ~25 — about 92% of those tensors is padding.

=> The real fix for a 3-gen window on this hardware is a ragged/sparse policy target in nnue-trainer (order-of-magnitude win), NOT more RAM. Suggest a follow-up bead against nnue-trainer.

Plan: attempt WINDOW=3 behind 'docker --memory 5g' (added to generation.sh, so an OOM kills the container and not another executor's arena/rustc — the box has no swap and the kernel OOM-killer would otherwise pick a victim by badness score). If it dies at 137, fall back to WINDOW=2 (gen6+gen7, ~238k rows) and complete the generation there — still 2x gen-6's data breadth, which is the bead's actual hypothesis.

Also: the first rounds driver was killed by a harness background-task cap at exactly 60 min, mid-round-B. Relaunched under setsid so the run owns its own session. Round A (gen5, seed 5011) completed clean before that: 119,161 rows / 1000 games, validate_rows.py OK, p1 565 / p2 435.
EXECUTOR FINDING 3 — WINDOW=3 CONFIRMED IMPOSSIBLE ON THIS BOX (empirically, not projected).

All three self-play rounds completed clean:
  work/gen5  seed 5011  119,161 rows / 1000 games  validate_rows.py OK
  work/gen6  seed 6011  117,973 rows / 1000 games  validate_rows.py OK
  work/gen7  seed 7011  120,004 rows / 1000 games  validate_rows.py OK
  pooled 357,138 rows / 3000 games

NOTE gen6's re-run produced EXACTLY 117,973 rows — bit-for-bit the same count gen-6 reported. So the rows really are reproducible from (net, seed), and gen6.md's caveat that PR #29's resign code would perturb the stream is FALSE when resign is off (it is off by default): control_draw() is a pure function of the game seed and consumes nothing from the per-ply stream. Losing rows costs an hour, not correctness.

WINDOW=3 train (357,138 rows) ran, completed epoch 1, and was OOM-killed at --memory 5g at the epoch 1->2 turn — exactly the 'shuffled = [t[perm] for t in train_t]' overlap predicted in FINDING 2. Container sat at 4.55-4.63 GB of the 5 GB cap through epoch 1, host down to 716 MB available. The cap did its job: the container died, not another executor's arena/rustc.

Epoch-1 datapoint worth keeping (log preserved at work/gen7/logs/train_window3_oom.log):
  WINDOW=3, 357k rows, epoch 1/8: holdout top-1 59.2%, value MAE 0.772
  vs gen-6's WINDOW=1, 118k rows, epoch 1/8: holdout top-1 56.4%, value MAE 0.810
=> more data DOES help, and it helps at epoch 1. That is evidence for the bead's hypothesis even though the full run did not fit.

Falling back to WINDOW=2 (gen6+gen7 = 237,977 rows, ~3.8 GB) and completing the generation there — still 2x gen-6's data breadth. Gauntlet 400 under the lock next. gen5's rows stay on disk for gen-8.
RESULT — gen 7 KEPT BACK at 0.480 over 400. PR #34 (draft). Nothing promoted or deployed.

  pooled 0.4800 (gate 0.55), 192-208-0 of 400
  headline 48.0% Wilson95 [43.1%, 52.9%], 0 capped, 0 stalled
  arena lock held for all 400 games; 192 FIXED sims, colour-paired, 4x100, seeds from 70011

KEY: this is NOT inconclusive like gen 6. gen 6's 0.4800 was over 100 games with 0.55 INSIDE [38.5,57.7]. At N=400 the interval is [43.1,52.9] and 0.55 is OUTSIDE it. At 192 sims the candidate is at best marginally worse than the gen-5 champion. Instrument known good (gen-6's control ran 0.850).

DIAGNOSIS POINTER — suspicion moves OFF data breadth, ONTO the training recipe:
  gen 6: window=1, 117,973 rows, N=100, 0.4800, top-1 peak 61.9%
  gen 7: window=2, 237,977 rows, N=400, 0.4800, top-1 peak 62.2%
Doubling the data moved top-1 by 0.3 points and the gauntlet by nothing. Two kept-backs at exactly 0.480 with a clean instrument, against the Java pipeline's FIVE straight promotions on the same architecture and same gauntlet. Chase, in order:
  (1) human-games curriculum at ~3x weight — Java mixed prod games into every training set, Rust is pure self-play. NOW UNBLOCKED: work/gamesdb/games.db (8.6 MB).
  (2) hyperparameters/epochs vs Java's — value loss still falling at epoch 8 (0.826->0.649) while top-1 plateaued and turned over at epoch 6; one epoch count serving neither head.
Also: self-play is p1-skewed 578/422.

SCOPE CUT: the bead's 3-generation window was NOT delivered. All three rounds WERE played and validate clean — 357,138 rows on disk (119,161+117,973+120,004, seeds 5011/6011/7011) in the MAIN checkout work/, durable. The WINDOW=3 TRAINING does not fit: measured 1.85 GB peak at 119k rows, linear, ~5.5 GB at 357k vs 7.7 GB with no swap; OOM-killed at the epoch 1->2 turn. Host shutdown stopped the retry, so WINDOW=2 is INTERIM, not the specified run. Kept datapoint: WINDOW=3 epoch 1 top-1 59.2% vs gen-6's 56.4% — more data helps the fit early, just not strength by epoch 8.

The real blocker is padding, not RAM: policy target is (n,k) with k=MAX legal actions 326 vs MEAN 25 => ~92% padding. Ragged/sparse targets in nnue-trainer would cut the footprint ~10x and unblock WINDOW=3 on this hardware.

FOLLOW-UPS to file: (a) curriculum from work/gamesdb/games.db; (b) audit epochs/lr/value-weight vs Java's 5 promotions; (c) ragged/sparse policy targets in nnue-trainer; (d) re-run gen 7 as 3-window + curriculum once (a)+(c) land.

close_reason: Merged PR #34. GEN-7 KEPT BACK — decisively (unlike gen-6): 0.4800 pooled over 400 games [43.1,52.9], 0.55 OUTSIDE the interval; instrument known-good. Diagnosis: data breadth hypothesis weakly supported at best — doubling rows (118k→238k, window 1→2) moved top-1 by 0.3pt and the gauntlet by NOTHING. Suspicion moves to the training recipe: (a) human-games curriculum x3 (Java's gen-5 promoted WITH it; now unblocked via recovered games.db), (b) epochs serve neither head (value loss still falling @8, top-1 peaked @6), (c) policy target is 92% padding (k=326 vs mean 25 legal — ragged targets = ~10x trainer memory cut; WINDOW=3 at 357k rows OOMs at 5.5GB/7.7GB because of it), (d) selfplay p1-skew 578/422. ASSETS: all 3 selfplay rounds (357,138 rows, seeds 5011/6011/7011) validated clean and BYTE-REPRODUCIBLE from seeds (gen-6 replay reproduced its exact 117,973 rows — resign-off perturbation caveat in gen6.md is false); rows die with this host but regenerate in ~3h. generation.sh hardened: trainer --memory cap, pre-flight window sizing, absolute WORK, lock reporting fix. title: Cross-play has no opening randomisation: 400 games are ~65 samples
description:
Found running S1 (vsbot-x70) with the diversity diagnostic added by vsbot-t3q.1.

A cross-play run's game count is not its sample size. The S1 run played 400
games and contained only 65 distinct ones; the greedy-vs-GoBot run that
produced the 49-1 played 12 and contained 5. Nothing randomises the opening and
both deployed engines play argmax with no root noise, so a run replays a small
set of games and any interval computed from the game count is far too narrow.

This is now the binding constraint on every cross-play number. S1 cleared its
>=0.55 bar at pooled 0.5875, but over the effective 65 samples the interval is
[46.3%, 69.6%] -- it straddles 0.55 and 0.50 -- so it could not be recorded as
a championship. superiority.md Gate B (never regress against the Go bot) has
the same problem.

Neither side exposes a usable lever today:
* vsbot MCTS runs mode=play(no-dirichlet,argmax-visits); MCTS_SEED does not
  perturb it.
* The Java live MCTS path hard-codes root noise off (GameLoopHandler
  loadMctsConfig: 'Root noise stays OFF (play mode, the Config default)').
* The Go bot-hoster's BOT_EXPLORE_EPSILON applies to EVERY turn, not just the
  opening, so turning it on weakens the opponent throughout and biases the
  result the other way.

What the arena does instead: eps=0.15 over the first 8 turns, drawn from a
per-pair seed, so diversity is reproducible (see virus-arena gauntlet docs).
The cross-play equivalent needs an opening-only exploration window on at least
one side, ideally seeded.

ACCEPTANCE: a cross-play run of N games whose distinct-game count is close to
N, so the harness's low-diversity warning stops firing and a cross-play pooled
score can gate. Re-run S1 on it and record whether 0.5875 survives.

Prior art / evidence: docs/benchmarks.md sections 3a and 4; PR #13.
close_reason: Merged PR #22: seeded opening exploration on the vsbot side (ExploringEngine decorator, VSBOT_EXPLORE_EPS default 0 = deployed binary unchanged; position-derived coin after codex P1 fix — no thread-timing dependence; refused with ponder). Acceptance: 50/50 distinct games (was 5/50); fake 98% -> 22%, matching the arena greedy floor from the P2 chair — t3q.1 diagnosis confirmed by two independent harnesses. Reproducible schedule (8/10 byte-identical at same seed; wall-clock search explains the rest). title: ponder canary FAIL: quality regression + unmotivated neutral (rebase x batching suspect)
description:
OWNER CANARY VERDICT on prod ponder (2026-08-13): FAIL. "Much faster, seems more stupid, I won easily, neutral placing was absolutely not motivated." Live logs show 0 fallbacks and 0 panics, so answers came from genuine searches over the pondered tree — the quality regression is in the search itself.

PRIME SUSPECT: MctsSearcher::rebase (added in PR #15) interacting with the batched searcher (PR #14). Timeline: S2's 40-game soak ran on its own branch BEFORE #14 merged; ponder+batching(B=8, virtual loss) were never soak-tested together. Hypotheses to kill in order:
1. rebase() while vl/vl_visits are nonzero or a batch is mid-flight: re-rooting could orphan virtual-loss adjustments, leaving the new root subtree with poisoned Q values (systematically pessimistic/optimistic children -> confident bad moves, fast early-stop because a corrupted leader looks uncatchable).
2. rebase() into the WRONG child (action-id mismatch between the opponent action decoded from the snapshot and the tree edge, esp. for PlaceNeutrals edges: flat pair ids 144 + i*144 + j) -> the bot searches a position that is not the actual position, then early-stops on garbage. The "absolutely not motivated" neutral placement is consistent with a tree rooted at a stale/wrong state.
3. Early-stop miscalibration on warm trees: visit counts inherited from ponder make the leader look uncatchable within the remaining per-action budget, so the bot answers almost instantly ("much faster") from a tree whose top move was optimized for a DIFFERENT predicted opponent reply distribution. Even without corruption, inherited visits + tight uncatchability math can lock in premature argmax.
4. Dirichlet/noise or exploration state leaking into play-mode ponder sessions (should be none — verify).

REPRO PLAN (do this before any fix):
- Local soak vs the LOCAL Go server: ponder=on + batching B=8 (current prod config) vs ponder=on + batch_size=1 vs ponder=off, >=40 games each arm. If B=8+ponder is the only weak arm -> hypothesis 1. Fixed-sims self-gauntlet ponder-on-vs-off is the cleanest strength check (arena has fixed-time mode; a ponder arm needs the proto driver, so use the crossplay-style local-server loop instead).
- Instrument: on every turn_change, log (root_state_hash_of_tree, actual_snapshot_hash) — ANY mismatch proves hypothesis 2 instantly. Log inherited_visits at each of our actions and whether early-stop fired at <20% budget.
- The owner's actual lost game is in prod games.db (https://vs.wandergeek.org/data/games.db, player names SuperiorBot Bot 1079 vs the owner) — fetch it, replay to the unmotivated PlaceNeutrals, and run the current searcher at that position ponder-off: if ponder-off picks a sensible move at the same position, the position itself convicts the ponder path.

FIX + ACCEPTANCE: root-cause identified with the instrument evidence; fix; ponder-on-vs-ponder-off local gauntlet >=100 games showing ponder-on >= 0.50 pooled (it must never be WEAKER; the whole point is free compute); the state-hash instrument stays as a permanent cheap assertion (mismatch -> drop tree + log loudly, never search a wrong tree). Ponder stays OFF on prod until the owner re-canaries.
close_reason: Merged PR #21. Root cause was TWO defects, neither hypothesized: (1) re-root path_to was DFS with a 4096-apply budget vs ~34-branching -> gave up after ~3 actions, threw the tree away (fix: deepen by ply; 18/18 at 18 applies; live hit rate 99%); (2) StopUncatchable fired on inherited visits — age of tree, not convergence ('inherited=7326 sims=128 -> stop @37ms of 739ms' = the owner's 'much faster'; fix: lead<=sims, provably free cold, bit-identical for non-ponder). H1/H2 ruled out with permanent state-hash assertion (0 mismatches over 5168 live answers); the unmotivated PlaceNeutrals is NOT ponder — cold search and 10k-sim reference choose it too = GEN-5 NET WEAKNESS (bead filed). Gauntlet: ponder-on 0.750 [0.657,0.825]/100 pooled both seats (reduced-depth measurement, shared box). Hair-trigger rate 18.4%->2.5%. PONDER STILL OFF ON PROD — re-enable via automated gates (400-game + soak) per new policy. Deferred: inherited-visit decay (strength change, >=400 games), multi-ply re-root cost, PONDER_SIM_CAP.

description:

T1 leaf batching + in-tree parallelism with virtual loss (accept: >=2x sims/s at equal cores AND fixed-time self-gauntlet >=0.55/400 vs serial). Note PR #8 finding: shared-TT lazy SMP gained nothing on this 4-vCPU box — batching is the primary axis, threads secondary.

T3 Gumbel root selection for SELF-PLAY only (accept: policy-target quality A/B at 192-256 sims).
T4 resign threshold for self-play throughput (accept: false-resign <5% with 10% no-resign control).
ACCEPTANCE per item in the doc; nothing ships to the live bot without a fixed-time gauntlet.
notes:
S3-T1 MERGED (PR #14): forward_batch bit-identical to serial (assert_eq, both SIMD+portable); leaf batching w/ virtual loss (B=8 default — below lane width is a LOSS, B=2=0.63x); ParallelMcts fine-grained Relaxed atomics, no unsafe, threads=1 bit-identical to MctsSearcher; panic propagation fixed (codex). Bench: 2.21x sims/s at B=8 single-thread; thread numbers not honest scaling (shared box). Gauntlet: 55-45 pooled 0.5500 at 100 games [45.2,64.4] — bar met marginally, 400-game CONFIRMATION PENDING on a free box (run after S1's big run). Config::default now batch_size=8 -> bin+arena get batching for free; deadline overshoot ~1-2ms. T2 (DAG), T3 (Gumbel), T4 (resign) remain open.

Counterfactuals exact (search-count-based, load-independent; 26219 predicted = 26219 ran). Re-measure per generation as value heads sharpen (one command). REMAINING in this bead: T2 DAG (in flight), T3 Gumbel (queued behind T2).
T2 DAG MERGED (PR #26), default ON (gauntlet-decided): within-turn permutation merging on existing State::hash + full State equality confirm (collision = duplicate node, never wrong merge); root noise cannot leak (only children enter index); vl per-edge undisturbed; re-root rebuilds index. Acyclic BY RULES (strict lexicographic decrease of (empty,-fortified,-neutral)). Numbers: 890->1501 distinct positions at 1500 sims (1.69x effective widening, 92 merges); 400-game gauntlet DAG-on vs off: 223-177 = 0.5575 [50.9,60.5] — real gain, gate-eligible. T3 GUMBEL up as DRAFT PR #33 (branch vsbot-1uv-s3-t3-gumbel), default OFF,
NEGATIVE RESULT on move strength + one useful training-side finding. Bead is now
complete: T1 #14, T2 #26, T4 #29, T3 #33.

NUMBERS (400 games, fixed 192 sims, colour-paired, Gumbel self-play mode vs
PUCT+Dirichlet self-play mode; box shared throughout, load 2.4-4.7, but
fixed-sims is load-TOLERANT by construction so the result stands):
216W 184L 0D = pooled 0.5400, wilson95 [49.1%, 58.8%]. Bar is >=0.5500 and the
lower bound is under 50% -> does NOT clear. Ships default-off, resign precedent.
Seat split 96/200 as P1 vs 120/200 as P2 (real asymmetry; the colour pairing is
what cancels it out of the pooled figure).

POLICY-TARGET PROBE (390 shared positions, equal sims, mean 22.6 legal actions):
  gumbel pi' (completed-Q) 1.094 nats, support 22.6/22.6, top1=puct pv 51.8%
  gumbel pv  (raw SH)      2.077 nats, support 13.8/22.6, top1=puct pv 35.6%
  puct pv    (INCUMBENT)   1.909 nats, support 14.4/22.6
  puct pi'   (completed-Q) 1.137 nats, support 22.6/22.6, top1=puct pv 53.6%
THE FINDING WORTH KEEPING: gumbel pi' and puct pi' are essentially the same
object (1.094 vs 1.137 nats, both full support). The improved policy is a
property of the COMPLETED-Q TRANSFORM, not of Gumbel root selection -- so if we
want that target we can have it on the existing PUCT arm at zero risk. Filed as
the suggested follow-up. Raw sequential-halving visits are a WORSE-shaped target
than the incumbent: narrower support (13.8 vs 14.4) at higher entropy (2.077 vs
1.909), because halving spreads visits evenly across the candidate set by
construction -- flatness, not information. gumbel pi' agrees with gumbel pv's
argmax only 35.1%, which is why best_action() returns the schedule's argmax and
not max-visits.

pv MAPPING (documented decision, both lossy): the row schema has ONE target
field and Gumbel produces two things. GumbelPv::Raw (default) = literal visit
counts, discards completed-Q. GumbelPv::Improved = pi' quantised to integer
pseudo-counts summing to the visit total (largest remainder), schema-valid but
NOT literal visits. Carrying both needs a 10th field and a trainer change.

IMPLEMENTATION: sigma follows mctx qtransform_completed_by_mix_value (c_visit
50, c_scale 0.1, completed Q min-max rescaled to [0,1]) NOT the paper's bare
form -- with raw [-1,1] values and c_scale 1 the target measured effectively
one-hot (support 1.4 of ~23). Play mode structurally cannot enable it
(Config::play spells all three exploration knobs off; Dirichlet+Gumbel is a
panic; ParallelMcts REFUSES a gumbel config rather than ignoring it like dag,
because a silently-PUCT search would mislabel a training target).

TWO BUGS FIXED before the numbers: (1) sequential halving gave a candidate
per_action descents in a ROW, which under leaf batching collapse onto one
pending child -- burned ~1/6 of the budget in phase 0; fixed to round-robin
(what mctx does). (2) codex review P2, valid: rebase fed v_mix the child-visit
average instead of the root's own leaf value; fixed by storing leaf_value_abs
per node. Both have regression tests that fail on the old behaviour.

GATES: build/test/clippy -D warnings/fmt all green, 449 tests / 39 suites exit 0.
Determinism extended to the gumbel arm incl. end-to-end at 192 sims (shard re-run
byte-identical; shards-of-2 reassemble exactly). trainer/validate_rows.py run
READ-ONLY: raw OK, improved OK, mixed gumbel+PUCT generation OK.

KEY TRAINING-SIDE FINDING for gen-8: the completed-Q improved policy target is a property of the transform, NOT of Gumbel root selection — computable off the existing PUCT arm (1.137 vs 1.094 nats, same support), zero risk, no root machinery; raw sequential-halving visits are a WORSE target (flatness, not information). S3-T1 (leaf batching + virtual loss + tree parallelism) is up as draft PR #14 (branch vsbot-1uv-s3-t1-batching). All in crates/virus-mcts; no other crate touched, no dep added.

WHAT SHIPPED
- PolicyValueNet::forward_batch: batch as the innermost axis ([channel][cell][8]). Same arithmetic in the same reduction order, so a batched result is BIT-IDENTICAL to the serial forward (asserted with assert_eq!, both SIMD and portable paths).
- MctsSearcher batches leaf collection: a round descends Config::batch_size times with virtual loss, evaluates the leaves in one forward_batch, backs them all up. Virtual loss lives in separate vl/vl_visits counters, so removal is an exact integer decrement and batch_size==1 is the serial searcher bit for bit.
- ParallelMcts (new type): workers over one shared tree. Fine-grained atomics (Relaxed per-edge n/w/vl), OnceLock for structure, no big mutex and no unsafe. Safe because the backup is absolute-frame -- W accumulates in one frame so a backup is a commutative add (invariant 1 doing real work). threads==1 is bit-identical to MctsSearcher; threads>1 is nondeterministic and opt-in, nothing gated on it.

comments.text:
S3-T2 (DAG transpositions) is up as draft PR #26 (branch vsbot-1uv-s3-t2-dag). All in crates/virus-mcts; no other crate touched, no dep added.

WHAT SHIPPED

Config::dag merges within-turn action permutations: an index from State::hash (the existing incremental Zobrist key, which per invariant 6 already carries movesLeft/neutralUsed/side/active) to node index, consulted when a child link is created. Every hit is confirmed by full State equality, so a 64-bit collision costs a duplicated node and never a wrong merge.

The four hazards, and why each is closed:
- Value merging is frame-safe because backup is absolute-frame (invariant 1): W means the same thing whichever parent a visit came through, so merging is a commutative add. A negamax tree would invert half the stats here.
- The DAG is acyclic BY THE RULES: every action strictly decreases the lex tuple (empty, -fortified, -neutral), so no position reaches itself and no two paths of different lengths can meet. Transpositions are strictly same-depth within-turn permutations.
- Dirichlet root noise cannot leak: only nodes created as CHILDREN enter the index, so nothing is ever redirected onto node 0, where the noised prior lives. rebase re-establishes this for the new root.
- Virtual loss is per EDGE, so merging nodes does not disturb T1's vl/vl_visits. What changes is that a merged node is more often already pending in the same batch, which the existing leaf-reuse path handles.

MEMORY / RECLAMATION. rebase's BFS already handled diamonds correctly (mapping guard), so node reclamation needed no change. The index WOULD have been worse than a leak if left alone — a stale key naming a discarded slot would merge a future child onto whatever now occupies that index — so it is rebuilt from the survivors on every re-root, skipping node 0. Index cost is one (u64,u32) per node vs a Node owning a whole State plus six ~34-wide vectors: a few percent.

NUMBERS (box NEVER idle, load 8-10, other executors concurrent)

Sim savings, examples/mctsbench, 1500 sims from a developed midgame (load-independent columns):
  B=1 DAG off: 1501 nodes,  890 distinct, 611 DUPLICATES (40.7%), 0 merges
  B=1 DAG on : 1501 nodes, 1501 distinct,   0 duplicates,        92 merges
  B=8 DAG off: 1501 nodes,  910 distinct, 591 DUPLICATES (39.4%), 0 merges
  B=8 DAG on : 1499 nodes, 1499 distinct,   0 duplicates,        92 merges
TWO OF EVERY FIVE expansions a plain tree pays for are a position it has already evaluated. The DAG's arena is duplicate-free, so the same 1500 expansions cover 1501 distinct positions instead of 890 — a 1.69x widening of what a fixed budget sees. Note it takes only 92 merges to produce that: a merge near the top stops a whole duplicate subtree from forming, so 'merges' and 'duplicates avoided' are different quantities.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the plan's wording: at a fixed sim budget the arena is the SAME SIZE either way (one simulation expands exactly one leaf). The DAG does not shrink the tree; it changes what the budget is spent on. Batching adds a smaller genuine node reduction (a merged node reached twice in one round is pending the second time).

ACCEPTANCE GAUNTLET, fixed sims (load-tolerant: contention makes it slower, never different — this is why batchgauntlet gained --sims), both arms at the default batch_size 8, colour-paired, 800 sims/action:
  100 games: 56W 44L 0D, pooled 0.5600, wilson95 [46.2%, 65.3%], 0 turn-cap games.
  DAG merges 14.1% of simulations; expansions -1.1% vs the plain arm.
Bar was 'no regression, >= 0.50'. MET at 0.5600 — which also clears T1's 0.55 bar. 100 games cannot RESOLVE 0.56 from 0.50 (the interval contains both); what it establishes is the absence of a regression, which is what T2 is gated on. 400-game confirmation running; result to follow.

Wall-clock sims/s is NOT a result here and is labelled as such: the same run's B=1 batch-sweep cell ranged 1573-2954 over five repeats. The index costs ~0.005% of a search (one lookup per node creation vs the net forwards).

DEFAULT: dag=true, gauntlet-decided, same precedent as T1 flipping batch_size to 8. CALLER-VISIBLE: Config::default() now carries dag:true, so the vsbot bin and the arena get it for free. Public API additive only (Config::dag, DEFAULT_DAG, node_count/distinct_positions/merges/key_collisions); no signature changed; every out-of-crate Config construction already uses ..Config::play().

NOT DONE (deliberate): ParallelMcts IGNORES Config::dag, the exact mirror of MctsSearcher ignoring Config::threads and documented in both places — the shared tree addresses nodes by Arc identity behind per-edge OnceLocks, so merging needs a concurrent index and an atomic create-or-adopt across two parents. Threads measured worthless on this box anyway (#8, S3-T1). parallel_with_one_thread_matches_the_serial_searcher now asks the serial side for dag:false so it keeps catching PUCT formula drift. docs/benchmarks.md and ARCHITECTURE.md left alone to avoid conflicting with concurrent PRs. T3 (Gumbel) and T4 (resign) not started.

comments.text:
S3-T4 (self-play resign threshold) is up as draft PR #29 (branch
vsbot-1uv-s3-t4-resign). All in crates/virus-selfplay; no other crate touched,
no dep added, ROW SCHEMA UNCHANGED.

VERDICT: resignation works and is honest, and is NOT worth turning on. It ships
DEFAULT-OFF with the numbers recorded. The bar it fails is the THROUGHPUT one,
not the accuracy one.

WHAT SHIPPED
- GameConfig::resign: Option<ResignConfig>, None by default, so every generation
  to date is bit-for-bit unaffected. A side resigns once the absolute-frame root
  value has been beyond `threshold` against it for `plies` of its OWN plies.
- z stays honest and absolute: a resigned game is scored "the side that did not
  resign won", NOT by the unfinished board's territory verdict -- which often
  still favours the side that gave up, because the rule fires on a search verdict
  running ahead of the board. Turn-cap/natural-end paths untouched.
- Resignation only truncates, never perturbs: the test reads root_value_abs()
  off the search the ply ran anyway and draws no randomness, so game g with
  resign on plays the same moves as game g with resign off and its rows are that
  game's rows truncated -- identical in every field but z.
- The hopeless counter is PER SEAT. One shared counter would look like a working
  feature and never fire: invariant 1 says the mover does not alternate, so the
  same far-negative value that means "p1 is lost" means "p2 is comfortable" one
  ply later, and a shared counter resets on every mover change.
- Config off unless --resign-threshold/RESIGN_THRESHOLD is given; --resign-plies
  and --resign-control-frac WITHOUT it are an error, not a silent no-op.
- Determinism unchanged and extended: control membership is mix64(game_seed ^
  SALT), a pure function of (seed, game index), consuming nothing from the
  searcher's stream. Re-sharding repartitions the arms rather than redrawing
  them, and every measurement counter re-sums identically across shard counts.

MEASUREMENT (96 sims, 2 shards, champion net, seed 40001; box NEVER idle --
gen-6 held two cores, load average 13-21 throughout, so all conclusions are read
off SEARCH COUNTS, which are exact and load-independent, not wall clock)

RUN A -- 240 games, 0.95/k=8, control-frac 1.0 (every game a counterfactual, so
240 measurement points instead of the 24 a production 10% arm gives):
  * 32.5% of games would resign (78/240)
  * FALSE-RESIGN 3/78 = 3.85%, wilson95 [1.32%, 10.71%]  -- bar <5%
  * mean plies saved per resigned game 21.8
  * searches saved 1621/27727 = 5.85% -> projected throughput gain +6.21%
    (doc bar at superiority.md:347-348 is >=20% saving)

RUN B -- the shipping config on the SAME 240 games, 0.95/k=8, control-frac 0.1:
  * resign arm 214 games, 72 resigned (33.6%) -- matches A's 32.5% counterfactual
  * THE COUNTERFACTUAL IS EXACT, TO THE SEARCH: A said 1621 searches would go if
    every game were in the resign arm; B held 26 games back as control, worth 113
    of those; 27727 - (1621-113) = 26219, and B ran exactly 26219.
  * False resignations measured STRAIGHT OFF THE ROWS, no counter arithmetic in
    the path: 71 games came out shorter and exactly 2 labels flipped
    (sp40001-25, sp40001-166, both played out to z=-1 but scored z=+1) = 2.82%,
    agreeing with A's 3.85%.
  * B's own 10% arm gave 6 would-resign events, 1 wrong = 16.7% [3.0%, 56.4%] --
    concrete proof that a production-sized control arm cannot resolve a 5% bar at
    this game count, which is why the measurement ran at control-frac 1.0.

RUN C -- 80 games, 0.80/k=6, control-frac 1.0 (does ANY setting clear the doc?):
  * 77.5% would resign; searches saved 21.78% -> +27.8% throughput, CLEARS >=20%
  * FALSE-RESIGN 4/62 = 6.45% [2.54%, 15.45%] -- MISSES <5%

THE FINDING: the two acceptance bars sit on OPPOSITE SIDES of the threshold knob
and no tested setting clears both. 0.95/k=8 is accurate (3.85%) and buys nothing
(5.85%); 0.80/k=6 buys enough (21.8%) and is not accurate (6.45%). Mechanism is
visible in the data: games here average ~115 plies (the doc's premise at
superiority.md:203-207 assumed ~55 actions), and the gen-5 value head does not
cross |v|>0.95 until roughly the last 22 plies -- the AZ threshold, tuned where
value heads saturate early, only ever reaches a short tail.

HONEST CAVEAT: neither measurement CONFIRMS anything, they bracket. n=78 and n=62
both have intervals reaching past 10%. Resolving a 5% bar at p-hat ~4% needs on the
order of 1000 resign events, i.e. ~3000 games at the 0.95 firing rate.

BEFORE THIS COULD BE ENABLED (not in this PR): (1) that ~3000-game run on a free
box; (2) a threshold sweep between 0.80 and 0.95 at k in 6..8 -- the crossover, if
one exists, is in that box. Everything needed to run both is in this PR: the flags,
the control arm, and an exact counterfactual.

title: search: enhanced alpha-beta stack (parity + enhancements)
description:
GOAL: virus-search — the enhanced iterative-deepening alpha-beta stack, parity-anchored then enhanced.

TWO-MODE DESIGN (copy Java's key trick): a plain mode that is byte-exact parity vs the fixtures, and an `enhanced` flag holding every strength feature. Parity mode is the oracle; enhanced is production.

PARITY FIRST: choose_depth must reproduce fixtures/gobot_search_parity.jsonl (412 records: move+score byte-exact) and choose_node_budget must reproduce fixtures/gobot_nodebudget_parity.jsonl. Read fixtures/gobot_search_parity.README.md for the record format. This requires identical child enumeration order from virus-core and identical TT semantics in parity mode (ply-exact probing, unbounded map ok there).

THEN ENHANCED (port from Java GoBotSearcher.java, 1465 lines — every feature is measured, do not improvise):
- staged movegen: TT-move-first fast path before materializing siblings; ttMoveTargetPlausible guard REJECTS PlaceNeutrals TT moves.
- packed array TT: single u64 payload (score 32 | depth 6 | flag 2 | generation 6 | action 18), lockless XOR-verified (keys[i]=key^data[i]), depth-preferred + generation-aged replacement, persists across moves (bump generation per move), cross-ply probing, mate-score rebasing to/from stored form. 2^21 entries.
- killers (2/ply, +5M) + history (per-mover per-cell, cap 9000, halved per search, quiet cutoffs only).
- move ordering tiers: TT +10M, killer +5M, win +1M, eliminations x100k, capture +10k, history <=9k, turn-continuation +100.
- turn-aware LMR: reduce 1 ply when searched>4 && order<10_000 && Move && child keeps mover; NEVER reduce turn-ending actions (assert counter==0 in tests).
- aspiration windows: delta=1500, widen 4x then full; off below depth 3 and in mate band.
- lazy SMP: N-1 helpers on the shared TT, staggered depths, full window, cap 4, env-off for gauntlets (make determinism a mode, not a memo).
- time management: soft deadline (skip next iteration past 55% budget), partial-iteration salvage guarded by bestScore > alphaOrig. INVARIANT: deadline path must return what choose_depth returns at the completed depth (write the consistency test — this exact bug cost the Java bot 0-10 live).
- wedge opening book (port Go opening_book.go): genuine first turn only (placed+movesLeft==3), void on collision.
- maximizing = state.current == root (max^n [i32;4] vectors for 3-4 players; no pruning there except exact mate cutoff).

ACCEPTANCE: parity fixtures byte-exact in plain mode; enhanced-vs-plain gauntlet using virus-arena stub or a minimal self-play loop showing enhanced >= plain at equal nodes (informational); NPS benchmark in PR (Java: 55-65k NPS; target 3x+); consistency test deadline==depth; LMR turn-ending counter test.

LANDMINES: ARCHITECTURE.md invariants 1,3,6. Fail-soft everywhere; TT bound flags on the min-branch are where the Java negamax rewrite was needed — port the Java (already-negamax-correct) logic, not old Go incumbent.

title: proto: WebSocket bot client + vsbot bin
description:
GOAL: virus-proto + vsbot bin — WebSocket bot client that plays clean games on a real server.

TRANSPORT: tokio + tokio-tungstenite. URL from env BACKEND_URL (default ws://localhost:8080/ws), append ?bot=true&namePrefix=$BOT_NAME_PREFIX. Reconnect with backoff. Keep the read loop free: searches run on a separate task so server pings are always answered (Java starved pongWait when searching on the read thread — copy their single-worker dispatch design).

MESSAGES (port from Go ~/Project/virusgame/backend/cmd/bot-hoster/bot_client.go — the most complete client — cross-checked with Java GameLoopHandler/HandshakeHandler): inbound welcome, bot_wanted, challenge_received, lobby_joined, game_start, multiplayer_game_start, game_state, move_made, neutrals_placed, turn_change, game_end, player_eliminated, lobby_closed, users_update. Outbound join_lobby, accept_challenge/decline_challenge, challenge, move{gameId,row,col,+diagnostics score/depth/nodesEvaluated/timeMs}, neutrals{gameId,cells:[2]}. Send a UUID requestId on every action (server supports idempotent replay; neither predecessor used it — we do).

STATE DISCIPLINE (ARCHITECTURE.md invariant 5): snapshot-authoritative. Every state-bearing message carries a full snapshot; decode+validate via virus-core; NEVER rebuild from deltas. Version counter: each accepted snapshot bumps position_version and cancels the in-flight search (CancellationToken); a search result is only sent if its version still matches AND game/seat/movesLeft guards still hold (re-validate at send time, both in the search task and the writer). Hash snapshots to suppress no-op updates (not DeepEqual).

description:
GOAL: virus-mcts — PUCT searcher + conv policy/value net inference; load the gen-5 champion and match Java's outputs, then beat its throughput.

NET (artifacts/mcts_champion.json, arch conv-policy-value-v1): 12x12x13 input planes -> 4 conv layers x 32 channels (3x3, ReLU) -> move head (per-cell logits) + factored pair head (pair logit = head_i + head_j + pair_bias) + value head (GAP -> 32 -> 1 tanh). Use f32 (Java uses double — f32 is fine for parity tolerance) with SIMD-friendly layout (im2col or direct conv with fixed 12x12; consider std::simd or manual unrolling; no external BLAS dependency needed at this size). FIX the known Java waste: policy and value must share ONE trunk forward per expanded node (Java re-runs the trunk in the value head — a free ~2x on self-play throughput).

title: virus-search: public stop flag so a superseded alpha-beta search can be aborted
description:
Codex review of vsbot-3ss (PR wiring ALPHABETA into the bin) raised a real P1 that could not be fixed inside that bead's territory.

PROBLEM: virus_proto::SearchBudget requires an engine to stop at its deadline AND poll is_cancelled. AlphaBetaEngine (crates/vsbot/src/alphabeta.rs) can only do the first: Searcher::search_with_deadline has no way to be interrupted, because Searcher::stop (an Option<Arc<AtomicBool>>) is private and used only to shut down lazy-SMP helpers. A superseded search therefore burns a core and holds its transposition table until its own deadline.

WHY IT WAS NOT FIXED IN vsbot-3ss: the fix belongs in virus-search, which was read-only territory for that executor. The two in-adapter workarounds are both worse: slicing the budget into short search_with_deadline calls restarts iterative deepening each slice and stalls at a fixed depth (a new iteration is not started past soft_deadline_percent of the budget it was given), and the node-budget entry is deterministic rather than wall-clock and would break the deadline/depth consistency the crate pins.

WHAT vsbot-3ss DID INSTEAD (mitigation, already merged): it hands over budget.deadline rather than the later ceiling, so a stale search dies at the target; and a search that finds the engine cache lock held (which IS the signal that a stale search is still running) takes a 2^18-entry table instead of the full 2^21, so overlapping searches cannot multiply the 32 MiB working set inside the deployment's 512 MB container. Documented in the alphabeta.rs module docs under 'Cancellation: what this engine can and cannot honour'.

PROPOSED FIX: give Searcher a public way to be handed an external stop flag — e.g. pub fn with_stop(Arc<AtomicBool>) or a stop field on SearchOptions — checked in the same Searcher::running() that already reads the SMP flag and the node limit. Then AlphaBetaEngine spawns a watcher off SearchBudget::cancel (or polls it) and raises the flag, and drops the CONTENDED_TT_LOG2 workaround.

ACCEPTANCE: a cancelled alpha-beta search returns promptly (a unit test in virus-search on the flag, and one in vsbot asserting choose() returns soon after the token fires rather than at the deadline); parity fixtures unchanged (412/412 search, node-budget); the deadline==depth consistency test unchanged.
close_reason: Merged PR #28: CancelToken generalised from the private lazy-SMP stop flag (cancel/is_cancelled/reset; SMP helpers adopt the caller's token), polled at the one shared budget site so cancellation is byte-for-byte a deadline expiry — invariant 3 inherited, not re-argued. Parity byte-identical (412+158), deadline==depth test untouched. AlphaBetaEngine bridges SearchBudget::is_cancelled via a scoped watcher w/ panic drop-guard (self-caught hang hazard, regression-pinned). JUDGMENT REVERSAL accepted: 4MiB contended-table bound KEPT (cancellation bounds overlap duration not count; OOM asymmetry in 512MB container), rationale rewritten. choose returns None when cancelled — stale moves never offered.

title: Investigate: live GoBot loses to vsbot GREEDY 49-1 while the offline oracle beats greedy 15-5
description:
Found while running the vsbot-e7h cross-play smoke.

MEASUREMENT A (cross-play, crates/virus-arena/crossplay/crossplay.py, 50 games):
  vsbot(SEARCH=GREEDY) vs the Go bot-hoster at 1s/move: 49-1-0, 98%.
  53 recorded games, ALL terminating 'no_moves' (real board endings, no
  forfeits/timeouts), median 41 turns. The Go bots demonstrably searched:
  2968 logged searches at depth 4-5, 5k-35k nodes each.

MEASUREMENT B (arena, colour-paired, same 12x12 board, 20 games):
  greedy vs ab-plain at depth:4 -> 5-15-0. Greedy scores 25%.
  ab-plain is the byte-exact GoBot oracle (fixtures/gobot_search_parity.jsonl,
  412 records), so A and B should be measuring close to the same opponent.

These disagree by far more than the known confound can explain. Cross-play
cannot balance colours (the server seats the challenger at P1, and only vsbot
challenges), so A carries a full first-mover advantage that B cancels by
pairing -- but first-mover advantage does not turn 25% into 98%.

CANDIDATES (none investigated):
- The bot-hoster configures its search differently from search.Choose at a
  fixed depth (different eval weights, budget, or move-ordering path).
- CPU starvation: 3 Go bots plus another gauntlet on a 4-core box. The depth
  4-5 log line suggests it, but starvation should not cost 98%.
- Something in the live protocol path costs the Go bot games it should win
  (a mishandled snapshot, a wasted turn, a bad neutral placement).
- The offline oracle and the deployed Go binary have diverged.

WHY IT MATTERS: superiority.md Gate B anchors the RL ladder to 'never regress
against the Go bot'. If the live Go bot is far weaker than its offline oracle,
that gate is anchored to the wrong bar and will pass candidates it should not.

REPRO: docs/benchmarks.md rows 1 and 3 carry both commands.
close_reason: Merged PR #13. VERDICT: 49-1 was a harness artifact, two compounding defects: (1) seat bias — colour-paired 200-game control: greedy 40.0% as P1 vs 25.0% as P2, P1 seat wins 57.5% overall; (2) DOMINANT: no opening randomisation -> 12-game rerun had 5 distinct games (P(true 12-0)~1.7e-5). Live Go bot verified healthy (734 searches depth 3-7, mean 15.3k nodes, attribution correct). Fixes: pooler rowid bug, orphaned-process teardown, crossplay --self-test now in CI, --direction alternate for Java (Go hoster structurally cannot alternate — refused with reason). Follow-up filed: vsbot-t3q.2 (opening randomisation).

comments.author: devbox
comments.text:
VERDICT (PR #13): the 49-1 was a harness artifact. The live Go bot never
diverged from its offline oracle, and no engine on either side is at fault.

RULED OUT (with evidence, not assertion):
* Diverged binary / differently-configured search. The hoster calls
  gamesearch.Choose under the 1000ms ProductionBudget -- the same searcher the
  ab-plain fixture pins. A 12-game re-run logged 734 searches at depth 3-7,
  median 4, mean 15,317 nodes; the arena's ab-plain at depth:4 spends ~30k
  nodes a move at the same depth. Same code path, same work.
* CPU starvation. Real (shared 4-core box) but the node counts above show the
  Go bot searching as much as the oracle it is compared against.
* games.db attribution. Verified against real rows: player1_name/player2_name
  carry "<prefix> Bot NNNN", result is the winning seat, and crossplay.py folds
  both seat orders to vsbot's perspective correctly.

CAUSE 1 -- one chair, and the chair is worth something. The server seats the
challenger at P1 (hub.go handleAcceptChallenge: Player1: challenge.FromUser)
and only vsbot challenges. Quantified with a 200-game colour-paired control
(greedy vs ab-plain d4, seed 777): greedy scores 40.0% (40/100) seated P1 and
25.0% (25/100) seated P2; the P1 seat wins 115/200 = 57.5% of all games. So
moving first is worth ~7.5 points (~52 Elo) and one-chair seating lifts greedy
25% -> 40%. Real, but it cannot produce 98%.

CAUSE 2 (dominant) -- the 50 games were not 50 samples. Nothing randomises a
cross-play opening and both bots play argmax, so the run replays the same game.
A 12-game re-run reproduced the anomaly exactly (12-0-0, 100%) over only 5
distinct games, opening identical across all twelve. At a true one-chair rate
of 40%, a genuine 12-0 has probability 0.4^12 ~ 1.7e-5 -- so the games were not
independent, and the published wilson95 [89.5%, 99.6%] was computed over a
sample size that did not exist. An eps=0 pair shows the mechanism: replay one
opening from both chairs and P1 wins BOTH -- greedy-as-P1 beats the depth-4
oracle, and the oracle-as-P1 beats greedy. Cross-play locked onto exactly one
opening and always played it from the winning chair.

HARNESS FIXES (crates/virus-arena/crossplay/, PR #13):
* --direction ours|theirs|alternate; `alternate` runs two phases and is the
  first colour-balanced cross-play mode. Verified end to end: in phase 2 the
  Java bot sends the challenge and vsbot logs "started as seat 2".
* theirs/alternate are REFUSED for --opponent go, with the reason. The
  bot-hoster's challenger targets Manager.IsAcceptor(userID), false for every
  id outside its own pool, so it structurally cannot challenge vsbot. This is a
  bot-hoster limitation, not a config gap; the alternative was to keep emitting
  one-chair numbers labelled as balanced.
* Distinct-game count (move-sequence fingerprint, wall-clock duration stripped)
  plus a warning when replays dominate -- the guard rail that would have caught
  this. Per-seat win rates and a pooled (W+0.5D)/N score in every report.
* --opponent java runs the Java champion in docker, for S1 (vsbot-x70).
* crossplay_pool.py shards a run across independent servers and pools it,
  unioning distinct games rather than summing them.
* crossplay --self-test, run by tests/crossplay.rs, covers the seat fold, the
  disconnect discard, the red-flag count and the fingerprint in CI. Leaving
  that logic uncovered is how 49-1 got published.

DEFERRED: cross-play still has no opening-randomisation lever, so even a
colour-balanced run's games are largely replays. Until one exists, the
distinct-game count -- not the game count -- is the sample size. Recorded in
docs/benchmarks.md "What is not measured yet".

title: strength: superiority design (RL ladder in Rust, time mgmt, parallel MCTS)
description:
GOAL: the superiority track — design doc + phased plan for making vsbot strictly stronger than the gen-5 Java champion, the Go bot, and the owner. DESIGN FIRST, code in follow-up beads.

CONTEXT (all prior research, do not re-derive):
- NNUE distillation is a dead end (4 failures documented in ~/Project/nnue-trainer/docs/; labels are the binding constraint; fixed-depth labels are trapped at their depth).
- Self-play RL (AlphaZero-style) is the proven winner: gen-5 champion promoted 5 consecutive times, 55.5-69% per generation. Blueprint: ~/Project/nnue-trainer/docs/plans/20260807-mcts-az-feasibility.md; per-generation pipeline: scripts/mcts_selfplay_gen.sh (selfplay -> curriculum -> train -> gauntlet -> promote, gate 0.55, window 3, curriculum on human games x3).
- The Java trainer (python/mcts/train_selfplay.py) is reusable as-is if vsbot emits the same row schema: {g, sym[144], ml, nuo, nux, mover, pi, pv, z(absolute frame)}.

LEVERS TO EVALUATE IN THE DESIGN (ranked by expected Elo/effort using the beads history):
1. Raw throughput: Rust sims/s >> Java (measure after virus-mcts). More sims at 1s/move is immediate Elo. Also the server allows 120 s/move and both predecessors used 1s — a principled time manager (remaining-clock aware, ponder?) is untapped Elo.
2. Continue the RL ladder in Rust: self-play generation in Rust (faster => bigger generations), train with the existing python trainer, gauntlet in virus-arena, promote into artifacts/. Curriculum from vs.wandergeek.org games.db (owner's human games — the explicit target opponent).
3. Search upgrades on the MCTS side the Java v1 skipped: tree/root parallelism with virtual loss, leaf batching, transposition-aware DAG (GoState.hash exists), Gumbel root selection, resign threshold for self-play throughput.
4. Hybrid: alpha-beta with policy-net move ordering (ordering_policy.json is vendored) as a fallback/second opinion; MCTS+AB ensembling is unexplored.
5. Bigger net (channels/layers) once Rust throughput headroom exists; gen-5 is only 4x32.

DELIVERABLE: docs/plans/superiority.md with feasibility verdicts, compute budget (local machine + what the owner's server nightly window offers), a phased bead breakdown, and the promotion gate definition (>=400 games, >=0.55 pooled vs current champion AND never regress vs the hand-tuned bar AND vs Go bot). The OWNER is the final judge — canary-first policy (virusgame docs/nnue-canary.md Goodhart lesson: gate wins did not transfer to beating the human).

DEPENDS: virus-mcts, virus-arena.

title: arena: gauntlet harness + cross-play vs Go/Java bots
description:
GOAL: virus-arena — the gauntlet/statistics harness. This is how every strength claim gets made; port the discipline, not just the code.

PORT (from Java train/GauntletMatch.java + Go backend/arena/):
- Color-paired even game counts; pair (2k,2k+1) shares an opening seed so identical sides cancel exactly.
- Seed derivation: SplitMix64 mix of (seed ^ 0x9E3779B97F4A7C15 * (game/2+1)) — nearby seeds must NOT replay overlapping openings (bead riy lesson).
- Seeded epsilon-greedy openings (eps=0.15, first 8 turns) for diversity against deterministic engines.
- Budget modes: node_limit (default 60k), fixed_depth, move_millis.
- Polymorphic sides via a trait: AlphaBeta(handtuned), Mcts(champion), plus per-side enhanced flags for search A/B.
- Wilson 95% intervals; draws NOT counted as half-wins in the headline; report W-L-D + interval.
- Discipline constants: gates are >=400 games (SE ~2.5pt); refuse to print a verdict on <100 games (emit "informational only").

CROSS-PLAY HARNESS: a script or subcommand that boots the local Go server + Go bot-hoster (GoBot prefix, deterministic) + vsbot, polls games.db for vsbot-vs-GoBot rows above a rowid baseline, reports win rate (port the pattern from ~/Project/nnue-trainer/eval_java_vs_go.py). Same for vsbot-vs-JavaBot (nnue-trainer jar with SEARCH=MCTS).

ACCEPTANCE: rust-vs-rust gauntlet runs deterministically at fixed seeds+node budget (SMP off) and reproduces byte-identical W-L-D across two runs; cross-play harness documented in README and demonstrated with a >=50-game smoke run vs the Go bot (report the number, informational).

DEPENDS: virus-search, virus-mcts.
notes:
IN PROGRESS (PR #12, draft, branch vsbot-e7h-arena-gauntlet).

Shipped in crates/virus-arena:
- rng.rs: SplitMix64 mix64 + Java's exact seed derivation
  mix64(seed ^ GOLDEN * (game/2+1)). Pair index, not game index.
- stats.rs: Go's Wilson95 constant-for-constant; draws never half-wins in
  the headline; >=400 / <100 discipline as a type (Verdict) that prints
  INFORMATIONAL ONLY rather than a claim.
- engine.rs: Side trait. Greedy / ab-plain / ab-enhanced / mcts. Per-side
  budgets. FIXED-TIME mode alongside nodes and depth (superiority.md S0),
  deadline-enforced per action with worst overrun reported.
- gauntlet.rs: colour-paired games rounded up to even, seeded eps-greedy
  openings, turn cap as a draw, threaded workers folded in index order.
- src/bin/arena.rs: the CLI, no new workspace dependency.
- crossplay/crossplay.py + tests/crossplay.rs (VSBOT_CROSSPLAY=1 gated).
- tests/determinism.rs: the gate.

Numbers pending; see the PR body and docs/benchmarks.md when it lands.

=== RESULTS (PR #12, draft, branch vsbot-e7h-arena-gauntlet) ===

CARGO GATES: fmt/clippy -D warnings/test --workspace all green, 0 failures
(parity fixtures included). virus-arena adds 39 unit + 4 determinism tests.

DETERMINISM GATE -- PASSES on the real headline run, not just the unit test.
100 games, seed 11, nodes:60000, SMP off, --threads 4 vs --threads 1:
diff of the 100 --per-game records + 5 summary lines = 105 lines identical,
exit 0. Only elapsed differed: 495.8s (4 threads) vs 1568.7s (1 thread).
tests/determinism.rs also pins that a config played against itself reads
exactly 50% (both games of a colour pair are literally the same game).

(1) ab-enhanced:n60000 vs ab-plain:n60000, 100 games, seed 11
    W-L-D 53-47-0   win rate 53.0%   wilson95 [43.3%, 62.5%]
    pooled 0.5300   margin +6   elapsed 495.8s   INDICATIVE (not gateable)
    Interval spans 50%. NOT evidence the stack does nothing -- this is equal
    NODES, and the stack buys better nodes-per-node / time-to-depth. Java's
    +64% was measured at equal TIME.

(2) mcts[mcts_champion]:1000ms vs ab-enhanced:1000ms, 100 games, seed 20260813
    W-L-D 93-7-0   win rate 93.0%   wilson95 [86.3%, 96.6%]
    pooled 0.9300   margin +86   worst deadline overrun 11ms of 1000
    elapsed 1437.4s   INDICATIVE (not gateable)
    *** The project's first Rust-vs-Rust cross-family strength datapoint. ***
    The gen-5 champion dominates the hand-tuned enhanced AB bar at equal wall
    clock. Consistent with the Java history, now without the cross-language
    confound. 400 games is ~1.6h on this 4-core box -- only time blocks it.
    Caveats recorded in docs/benchmarks.md: ab-enhanced does not spend its
    full second (soft_deadline_percent=55 is its production time manager);
    work_a is NOT sims/s (a sim hitting a known-terminal node returns a
    cached value without touching the net, so won endgames inflate totals).
    Sustained throughput from virus-mcts's own mctsbench: 3799 net-value
    sims/s, 0.249 ms per fused net forward under AVX2.

(3) CROSS-PLAY vsbot(GREEDY) vs GoBot, 50 games, through the real Go server
    W-L-D 49-1-0   win rate 98.0%   wilson95 [89.5%, 99.6%]
    seats 50 P1 / 0 P2   INFORMATIONAL ONLY
    Plumbing confirmed: 53 recorded games, ALL terminating no_moves (real
    board endings), median 41 turns; Go bots demonstrably searching (2968
    searches, depth 4-5, 5k-35k nodes). 3 shutdown-race disconnects discarded.
    DO NOT read 98% as strength. Cross-play structurally cannot balance
    colours (server seats the challenger at P1; only vsbot challenges), and
    the arena DISAGREES: colour-paired greedy vs ab-plain (the byte-exact
    GoBot oracle) at depth:4 goes 5-15-0, i.e. greedy scores 25%.
    -> Filed as bd vsbot-t3q.1. Matters because superiority.md Gate B
       anchors the RL ladder to "never regress against the Go bot".

CODEX REVIEW: 2 findings, both real, both fixed (01b8921):
  [P1] the move clock started AFTER building the searcher, so the enhanced
       arm's 32MiB TT allocation and the plain arm's per-move rebuild were
       unmetered -- handed to exactly the arm being compared to MCTS at equal
       wall clock. Clock now starts first; MCTS already timed root expansion.
  [P2] --max-turns/--explore-turns were derived as turns*3 plies (copying
       Java). PlaceNeutrals spends a whole turn in one action, so games with
       placements overran both limits. Now counted from real seat changes.
Four more found by RUNNING the harness: MCTS arm was on Config::play()
(hand-tuned leaf value -> would have reported the champion while playing
priors-only, and ~24x cheaper per sim so it would have flattered throughput);
a Searcher takes its root player from the state it is built with, so building
both arms at game start gave seat 2 a seat-1 searcher (now lazy + regression
test); cross-play counted shutdown disconnects; an explicit [[bin]] path names
a file absent from the Dockerfile's stub cache layer (now auto-discovery).

DEFERRED (honest):
- Nothing at 400 games. Only wall clock blocks it; harness labels every row.
- Cross-play ran SEARCH=GREEDY: vsbot's build_engine still rejects ALPHABETA
  and MCTS (concurrent engine-wiring bead). Script takes --search, no change
  needed when that lands.
- No Java cross-play arm: no JVM on this host, so it could not have been run.
  Shipping an untested boot sequence would be worse. Structure takes a 3rd arm.
- Two different net artifacts in one gauntlet: REFUSED with an error, not
  approximated. Needs a second loaded net threaded through the sides.
- --vsbot-instances > 1 wastes ~half its games to vsbot-vs-vsbot sparring
  (excluded by the name filter, never miscounted). Documented, not fixed.
- Did not touch crates/vsbot or crates/virus-proto beyond reading them.

title: BLOCKER (server-side): prod games.db stopped persisting 2026-08-09 — curriculum starved
description: Owner copied /home/devbox/games.db (2026-08-14); it is byte-identical (md5 e5be7cc00f343d4b555dab8ece32427a) to the published https://vs.wandergeek.org/data/games.db and still ends at started_at 2026-08-09 19:01:04 with ZERO SuperiorBot rows — despite SuperiorBot demonstrably playing prod games on 08-13 (server acked wins; owner played it). The backend writes and serves the SAME file (virusgame/backend/main.go:10 runtimeDBPath=data/games.db), so this is not a stale export: the backend itself stopped persisting finished games on Aug 9 — around the gen-5 redeploy window. Persistence path is the fail-closed outbox (backend/outbox.go); a wedged outbox or a swapped/unmounted volume would look exactly like this. IMPACT: Java nightly curriculum starving since Aug 9; our S5 curriculum lever and the owner-game probe (vsbot-07x caveat) blocked; games played since Aug 9 likely unrecoverable if never written. FIX IS SERVER-SIDE (owner): on the host, check (1) docker logs of the virusgame backend for sqlite/outbox/persist errors, (2) mtime + path of data/games.db inside the backend container vs the volume actually mounted, (3) disk space. Caveat: prod runs source ahead of the repo (nnue-trainer-1jh.5), so file layout may differ.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND 2026-08-14 (not a persistence failure): the backend is healthy — /diag shows persist_status=ok, outbox_depth=0, last_success minutes ago; /last_games returns today's games incl. SuperiorBot. The DB runs journal_mode=WAL (storage.go:33): the main games.db file froze at the last checkpoint (Aug 9, the redeploy restart) and every write since lives in games.db-wal (~4MB) — constant reader traffic starves SQLite's auto-checkpoint. The public /data/games.db export serves only the main file, so every naive fetch (owner's copy, Java trainer's GAMES_URL nightly fetch) sees Aug 9. RECOVERY (done): fetched /data/games.db-wal alongside the main file — sqlite replays the WAL on open; full fresh DB (2041 games, 30 SuperiorBot rows incl. owner's games) checkpointed locally at work/gamesdb/games.db. SERVER FIX (owner, one-liner, ideally cron'd nightly before the 03:00 trainer window): sqlite3 <data-volume>/games.db 'PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);' — folds WAL into the main file so the export goes fresh. Until then the Java trainer's curriculum stays starved (its fetch gets only the main file); OUR pipeline is unblocked (we fetch both files).
